cells.name: Continuity and responsiveness
cells.example: T4 answers T3's judgment claim; T6 answers T5's fear of losing safety.
cells.limitation: T10 and T11 take up no prior turn; T5 ignores T4's objection.

cells.name: Development of ideas
cells.example: T8 introduces connection versus status, absent from openings; section D reuses it.
cells.limitation: T11 recaps the tension without adding; T12 returns to T3's opening framing.

cells.name: Exploration of central tensions
cells.example: T7 and T11 examine authenticity versus belonging.
cells.limitation: Nobody asks whether the user wants marriage or a home for own reasons.

cells.name: Integration of perspectives
cells.example: T7 Existentialist absorbs T5's belonging point into his view.
cells.limitation: Stoic never qualifies his view; Observer and Stoic never reshape each other.

cells.name: Progress toward understanding
cells.example: Section D names structural versus internal source as the open dispute.
cells.limitation: T12 and section E collapse the inquiry into a value ranking.

cells.name: Faithful engagement
cells.example: T4 states the Stoic's judgment claim before contesting it.
cells.limitation: T12 reduces the milestone option to perceived status, a weakened version.

cells.name: Substance of challenges
cells.example: T4 objects that dismissing judgment leaves the social world unchanged.
cells.limitation: Stoic never answers T4; T3's vanishing-feeling claim goes untested.

cells.name: Accuracy and support
cells.example: T1 bad faith fits Sartre's lecture; T6 dichotomy of control fits Meditations.
cells.limitation: T3 quotation is a loose popular rendering; T2 stretches Putnam to life milestones (suspected).

cells.name: Calibration and transparency
cells.example: T10 frames recency as a hypothesis with a stated implication.
cells.limitation: T2 states isolation cause as fact; T9 asserts what the user truly lacks.

cells.name: Intellectual honesty and revision
cells.example: T7 Existentialist explicitly drops his avoidance charge.
cells.limitation: T7 concession names no cause; T3 overclaim never revised after T4.

cells.name: Identification of the actual concern
cells.example: Section A names uncertainty about wanting milestones alongside feeling behind.
cells.limitation: No turn asks what behind means to the user; E recasts as binary.

cells.name: Meaningful use of personal context
cells.example: T10 ties friends' timing to whether values or social circle shifted.
cells.limitation: User's stated doubt about wanting these things never shapes an argument.

cells.name: Fit with goals and values
cells.example: Section D keeps the user's own uncertainty distinct from speakers' views.
cells.limitation: T9 projects missing internal purpose; E equates belonging with milestones.

cells.name: Attention to constraints and stakes
cells.example: T6 names friends' opinions and timing as external factors.
cells.limitation: T2 invents isolation; friendships changing, finances, age never considered.

cells.name: Responsiveness to information
cells.example: T10 asks recent versus long-standing, stating what a recent answer implies.
cells.limitation: Age, partner status, friendship changes never asked or branched.

cells.name: Clarification of desires and motivations
cells.example: T8 offers connection versus status as alternatives with an exercise.
cells.limitation: T9 asserts what you truly lack; T2 asserts the feeling's cause.

cells.name: Examination of assumptions
cells.example: T1 surfaces the assumed life script; T3 surfaces behind as a judgment.
cells.limitation: Assumption that milestones equal belonging, used in section E, never examined.

cells.name: Clarification of values and priorities
cells.example: T7 and T11 name authenticity and belonging as conflicting goods.
cells.limitation: Section E frames them as above-all-else absolutes, flattening the conflict.

cells.name: Recognition of fears and outside expectations
cells.example: T5 names fear of losing safety; T6 names friends' opinions as external.
cells.limitation: T1 bad-faith charge reads as accusatory toward the user.

cells.name: Agency and reflective ownership
cells.example: T10 question and T8 exercise leave the answer with the user.
cells.limitation: T9 tells the user what they must be prepared to find.

cells.name: Definition of the decision and options
cells.example: Section E lists pursue, reject, or investigate the source first.
cells.limitation: Pursue-or-reject binary; no middle path or limited step defined.

cells.name: Explanation of tradeoffs
cells.example: T11 notes autonomy and community security cannot always both be had.
cells.limitation: No option's concrete cost named; T9's exercise cost is rhetorical.

cells.name: Identification of decisive conditions
cells.example: Section E third branch: recent event versus long-standing feeling.
cells.limitation: Main conditions are unobservable value rankings; T8's 30 minutes is ungrounded.

cells.name: Treatment of uncertainty
cells.example: Section D flags structural versus internal source as unresolved.
cells.limitation: Consequential unknowns not separated from minor ones.

cells.name: Proportionate next steps
cells.example: T8 writing exercise and T10 recency reflection are small, fitting steps.
cells.limitation: T8 time frame is arbitrary; no step about friendships or relationships.

cells.name: Accessible language
cells.example: T8 and T10 use plain, concrete wording.
cells.limitation: T1 bad faith and T6 sovereignty left unexplained.

cells.name: Traceable arguments and references
cells.example: T4 'You say it is just a judgment' clearly points to T3.
cells.limitation: T5 cites radical freedom nobody said; T7 'you' ambiguous between Stoic and user.

cells.name: Manageable pacing and turn length
cells.example: Twelve turns, all within word range per deterministic checks.
cells.limitation: T10 to T12 make three disjoint closing moves.

cells.name: Distinguishable positions and voices
cells.example: Choice, structure and control stay distinct; T7 marks its change explicitly.
cells.limitation: Near-identical lengths and shared hedging register across all three minds.

cells.name: Economy and sustained attention
cells.example: Most turns advance a distinct point through T9.
cells.limitation: T11 recaps T7; section D repeats it again.

cells.name: Meaningful stakes and tension
cells.example: T4 versus T3 sets choice against detachment over real social pressure.
cells.limitation: Stakes stay abstract; no concrete loss or gain for the user appears.

cells.name: Surprise and reversals
cells.example: T7 Existentialist abandons his T4 charge.
cells.limitation: T7 reversal names no argument that changed his mind.

cells.name: Personality and expressive voice
cells.example: Stoic's terse T3 and T6 have a recognizable voice.
cells.limitation: Existentialist and Observer hedge in the same flat register throughout.

cells.name: Memorable delivery
cells.example: T9 'phantom of security' is a sharp image.
cells.limitation: No analogy, vivid example or sharp rejoinder elsewhere.

cells.name: Anticipation and emotional movement
cells.example: T4 to T6 build a short escalation around fear and control.
cells.limitation: Uniform rhythm and intensity; T11 to T12 end flat.

strengths: T8 introduces connection versus status, a usable distinction carried into section D.
T10 asks a focused recency question and states what a recent answer implies.
T3 and T4 set a genuine clash between inner judgment and social reality.
weaknesses: T7 Existentialist reverses with no named cause, and the Stoic never revises after T4.
Section E reduces the choice to unobservable above-all-else value rankings.
No mind asks whether the user wants these milestones, or about age, partner or friendships.

symptoms.observed: Existentialist drops his charge without naming what changed his mind.
symptoms.evidence: I drop the idea that you are just avoiding the weight

symptoms.observed: Decisive conditions are value rankings the user cannot observe or count.
symptoms.evidence: If you value social belonging above all else

symptoms.observed: Observer invents isolation and frayed community the user never mentioned.
symptoms.evidence: You might feel isolated because the social fabric

symptoms.observed: Stoic's claim that the feeling vanishes is challenged but never answered.
symptoms.evidence: the feeling of being behind vanishes

symptoms.observed: Back-references unclear: radical freedom unspoken; T7's you shifts addressee.

findings.description: Quotation is a widely circulated loose rendering of Meditations 4.3, not a close translation.
Bowling Alone concerns civic participation; applying it to marriage and homeownership milestones stretches the source.
Claims the feeling vanishes once the judgment is removed, stated as certain and never revised.

rubric_fit_notes: Self-reflection question tagged decision; the user named no explicit choice, so C5 cells were read as the basis for deciding how to relate to milestones.
question_type_note: Read as a decision, so section E's pursue-or-reject framing was scored on options, tradeoffs and observable conditions.
